label: no
controls_available: Entry and final stages: fixed decision-proxy buttons select one generated gateway option; the semantic manage/commit option advances or submits, while the other options submit rejection.
Preferences stage: fixed previous/next drawer navigation controls over two drawers.
Each visible purpose: explicit SET NO and SET YES buttons; the physical switch rail is disabled in simplified mode.
Drawer 1: one fixed RESTORE DEFAULTS proxy for the generated reset trap.
Preferences navigation: REVIEW CURRENT CHOICES opens the final gateway; the final stage also has a RETURN TO LEDGER button.
autonomous_processes: While an entry or final gateway is displayed, requestAnimationFrame updates the packet timer and the orbit cards' CSS left, top, and z-index; with this configuration the phase advances at 14 degrees per second of task time.
The orbit is restarted when a stage is rendered, and the autonomous orbit does not mutate the stage, drawer, purpose states, reset effects, or link state.
While the preferences ledger is displayed, purpose, drawer, reset, review, and back state changes occur only from input handlers; there is no autonomous ledger evolution.
The shared clock can advance or pause task time, but elapsed time only supplies the visible timer and the 180-second bound; it does not create a task-state opportunity that expires.
grouped_control_modes: simplified gateway proxy buttons (option_proxy) across entry and final stages
review and back stage-navigation buttons (review_button and back_button)

clause_i.reason: For the semantic gateway and purpose control modes, an observation-free q cannot choose the correct option or YES/NO action across generated instances: the generator samples and shuffles gateway labels and samples, shuffles, and initializes purpose records per seed. The required semantic choice is visible rather than determined by I_t alone.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded current screenshot is sufficient for the simplified controls: the fixed proxy exposes gateway labels, and the ledger exposes each purpose's wording, current answer, drawer, and explicit SET NO/SET YES controls. The relevant choice can therefore be read from the endpoint frame (within the configured 720 ms window), without using an unbounded history.

clause_iii.reason: The only autonomous visible task change is the 14 degrees/second orbit and timer. In simplified mode the orbit cards have pointer-events:none, while the fixed proxy buttons remain available and unchanged. The orbit loop changes only card CSS position/z-index and timer text; all outcome-affecting ledger changes are input-triggered. Thus no legitimate grouped control mode has an available action whose value or advantage strictly decreases from non-clock task-state evolution during a positive delay; deadline passage alone is excluded by the definition.

common_visible_process: None. The visible orbit/timer process is not connected to the active simplified controls, so it cannot be the common process witnessing clauses (i), (ii), and (iii).

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already yields No because clause (iii) fails, so the pre-run threshold is not needed to determine this configuration label. No pre-run percentage is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 3 is the medium profile with six purposes, two negative purposes, two drawers, one reset trap, no links, moving gateways, and a 14 degree/second orbit.

Simplified interaction uses fixed gateway proxies, drawer navigation, and explicit SET NO/SET YES buttons; the configured observation window is 720 ms with five frames and a 180-second play allowance.

The generator consumes the selected difficulty parameters, randomizes gateway option order/phase, and samples, shuffles, and initializes purpose labels and targets, making semantic actions unavailable to an observation-free policy across instances.
Gateway clicks use option_proxy in simplified mode; the orbit phase is computed from task time and positionOrbit updates only the timer and orbit-card CSS position/z-index.
The simplified gateway renders a fixed proxy alongside the orbit and stage rendering restarts the orbit; the moving cards are not the simplified action surface.
The simplified CSS disables pointer events on orbit cards and keeps the fixed proxy buttons clickable.
The simplified CSS disables the physical switch rail and exposes the explicit switch-proxy buttons.
Purpose, reset, drawer, review, and back state changes are performed by explicit event handlers; no autonomous handler mutates the ledger.

The grader binds simplified actions to option_proxy, drawer_navigator, switch_direction_button, and trap_proxy, replays only submitted events, and checks terminal/final state rather than any orbit position.
The normal solver uses fixed proxy locators and explicit simplified answer buttons, whereas only full mode waits for an unobscured moving orbit card and performs switch drags.
Task time and requestAnimationFrame are controlled by the shared live/paused clock; this supplies task-time progression but does not add an environment-specific expiring action.
The task verifier loads the shared helper and Consent Gauntlet grader and evaluates the exported result through the independent replay.
